title: QPS sagging — hypothesis capture + runbook notes
content:
Purpose
Quick capture from the 12/10 perf sync focused on the last 48h QPS sag observed on the egress pool (us-west-2b) and the micro-experiments we ran. This is a running notes doc — action owners and short experiment recipes only.

Summary of issue
- Symptom: sustained QPS drop from ~1.1k -> 650–800 for model-family: rw-13b-lt-quant during weekday peak windows (observed 2026-12-09 02:00–12:00 UTC). Tail latency mostly stable, but p50/p90 slipped and effective throughput fell: background traffic (embeddings) unaffected.
- Where: appears localized to a subset of hosts in us-west-2b (node tags: pool=egress, hw=4xA100-q8). Not observed in eu-west-1 or in dedicated-reserved pools.
- Change window: suspect change on 2026-12-08 23:40 UTC (small rollout of scheduler change + kernel selection tweak). Rollout PR: serving-runtime#2789 (linked).

Immediate data points (what we pulled during sync)
- Baseline (normal): sustained QPS 1100, avg per-host QPS 220, gpu_util 72%, p50=38ms, p95=122ms.
- Degraded: sustained QPS ~700, per-host QPS 115, gpu_util 84% (spikes to 96% on some hosts), p50=48ms, p95=210ms.
- Observed increased memcpy stall time in runtime traces for affected hosts (~+14ms median on hot paths).
- KV cache hit-rate unchanged at 87% overall but per-host hotness skew increased: top-5 prefixes on bad hosts show cache miss amplification.

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) Kernel selection regression (high confidence) — PR #2789 changed kernel pick heuristics for rw-13b variants; new kernels may push more device-to-device copies / require extra temporary buffers. Explains memcpy increase and higher GPU utilization.
2) Memory fragmentation / allocator pressure on affected instances — allocator metrics show increased external fragmentation on nodes with lower effective QPS. Could be caused by slightly larger intermediate tensor scratch from the new kernel path.
3) Orchestration-level throttling burst (lower confidence) — autoscaler observed short-lived flapping ~23:45 on 12/08; control-plane log shows scale-in/in-flight decision that could have overlapped with traffic burst and warmed hosts incorrectly.
4) NUMA imbalance on those host types after kernel switch (low confidence) — trace evidence limited but worth checking if device affinity changed in the new run.

Experiments run during the standup (notes + results)
- Shadow-run with kernel pinned back to pre-2789 (branch: release/2026-11-30): bench harness 'bench-run --profile=rw-13b-lt --concurrency=32 --duration=10m --pin-kernel=legacy'
  - Result: QPS restored to ~1.05k across same hosts, p95 reduced to 130ms. Strong signal in favor of hypothesis #1.
- Live canary rollback on 3 hosts (small subset) with kernel pinned: these hosts returned to expected throughput within 7 minutes of the rollback.
- Memory stress check: run 'alloc-scan --interval=30s --pidfilter=runtime' on 4 bad hosts for 2h
  - Result: fragmentation counters increased slowly but did not spike right at regression window. Suggests fragmentation is secondary effect if any.
- Autoscaler event replay: replayed the scale decision log on staging; did not reproduce flapping pattern. Control-plane logs show one failed API call during 23:46 (403) that triggered a fallback, but not sure it correlates.

Immediate actions (owners + due dates)
- Rollback: schedule a controlled rollback of the kernel-selection tweak for the remaining egress hosts tonight 12/11 02:00 UTC if no blockers — owner: Ravi (Jira JIRA-ENG-4721).
- Bisect: create a smaller bisect job that toggles just the kernel pick bit with A/B on the same host (no other changes) to validate causality — owner: Liam, due 12/11 EOD. Command template: 'bench-bisect --toggle kernel_pick_flag --runs 6 --traffic-profile peak'
- Telemetry: add a quick metric for 'memcpy-micros-per-inference' to the perf dashboard (short-term derived metric) and alert if > +8ms above baseline — owner: Jun, due 12/12.
- Patch: if bisect reproduces, prepare a revert PR and a smaller kernel change that preserves pre-2789 buffer usage patterns — owner: Sofia, draft PR by 12/12.
- Runbook update: add a short recovery checklist to the serving-runtime runbook: how to pin kernels, how to run bench-bisect, and quick KB around memcpy/stall diagnostics — owner: Maya, update by 12/14.

Things to capture for triage (data attachments to add)
- Per-host kernel selection logs (/var/log/serving/kernel-chooser.log) from 12/08 23:30–00:15 UTC for all affected hosts (Ravi to bundle).
- Bench-harness raw traces for at least two restored hosts and two degraded hosts (Jun to upload to S3: s3://redwood-perf/qps-sagging/2026-12-10/).
- Device-level NVTX slices from one affected host and one healthy host (Liam owns).

Open questions / unresolved
- Why is the cache hit-rate stable while some hosts show amplified miss patterns? Is the runtime cache routing or load-shedding interacting with the new kernel path?
- Were there any driver updates in the affected host pool around 12/08 (kernel driver / cuda minor releases)? Ops says no scheduled driver change but double-check.
- Is the memcpy latency observable inside the kernel implementation (i.e., introduced by extra copies) or by a different path (e.g., host->host DMA due to staging)? Need repo-level diff.

Quick reproducer notes (how to run locally in lab)
1) Boot lab host with same image as production: 'image: prod-2026-11-29-egress' and tag hw=4xA100-q8
2) Start bench harness: 'bench-run --profile=rw-13b-lt --seq-len=1024 --batch=1 --concurrency=64 --duration=15m'
3) Toggle kernel: from runtime binary, set env SERVE_KERNEL_PICK=experimental and restart runtime. Observe metrics in 2–5 minutes.
4) If pins: set SERVE_KERNEL_PICK=legacy, restart.

Communication plan
- Post a short summary to #perf with the rollback plan and high-confidence hypothesis after the rollback completes.
- Incident timeline: if rollback fails to restore throughput to >=90% baseline within 20m on pinned hosts, escalate to on-call SRE and post to #incidents.

Notes / meeting decisions
- Team agreed to prioritize rollback followed by a strict bisect before any additional kernel changes go to canary.
- No further changes to autoscaler or scheduling in the next 48h while bisect is in progress.

Appendix: small reproducer output excerpt (bench-run)
- Healthy host sample: 'avg_qps=220, p50=36ms, p95=118ms, memcpy_micros=18'
- Affected host sample: 'avg_qps=112, p50=47ms, p95=208ms, memcpy_micros=34'

If you add anything to this doc, please add your initials and timestamp for traceability.
